completeness: every pre-registered cell must be completed with the expected checkpoint SHA-256; otherwise the analysis refuses to run (no partial analysis).
cost_report: executed optimizer steps, processed examples, executed and nominal TFLOPs per arm (deterministic given the seed; reported, not tested), and the tuning cost: number of validation runs and their executed steps

decision_rule.1: p_holm < 0.05 and the whole 95% CI > 0  -> A superior
decision_rule.2: otherwise, the whole 90% CI inside (-delta, +delta) -> practically equivalent
decision_rule.3: p_holm < 0.05 and the whole 95% CI < 0  -> B superior

endpoint: acc_centralized at the last round, in percentage points; paired per seed (A - B)

interpretation.non_inferiority: Pre-specified secondary reading of the primary contrast: FedHAD is non-inferior to the tuned FedProx at margin delta iff the lower end of the 90% CI (one-sided 95%) of FedHAD - tuned is > -delta.
interpretation.primary_1: FedHAD more accurate than the tuned FedProx: the heterogeneity-driven policy beats generic less-aggressive optimization; the accuracy claim survives tuning.
interpretation.primary_2: Equivalent within +/- delta: FedHAD's accuracy is matched by tuning; the contribution must be framed as automatic, tuning-free budget selection (it reaches the tuned operating point without the validation grid). Compare costs: if the tuned FedProx also uses fewer steps, FedHAD does not dominate it.
interpretation.primary_3: Tuned FedProx more accurate: the reviewer's concern is confirmed; the accuracy benefit is attributable to less aggressive optimization, not to heterogeneity information; only the tuning-free argument (and its cost) remains.
interpretation.primary_4: Inconclusive: report the CI and non-inferiority result; no accuracy claim against tuned baselines may be made.

multiplicity: Holm within each family: primary = the primary contrast at both alphas (2 tests); secondary = the secondary contrasts at both alphas (4 tests).
question: Is FedHAD's final accuracy explained by heterogeneity-driven allocation, or is it matched by a uniformly less aggressive FedProx (lower lr / fewer epochs) selected on separate validation seeds?
substrate: CIFAR-10, 5 clients, 10 rounds, FedProx mu=0.01, batch 32, common initial checkpoint per seed
tests: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (zero_method=wilcox); percentile bootstrap CIs of the mean (10000 resamples, seed 20260930); TOST Wilcoxon against +/- delta reported
title: R2 experiment 2 — definitive evaluation: FedHAD vs tuned FedProx
